g.text: Who pays under co-tenancy: the memory-bound and latency-critical victims absorb the slowdown; the compute-bound victim is nearly immune
Cells = measured victim slowdown S (co-run / solo) + the mechanism. Thor values shown; Orin in parentheses where it differs. All streams, CPU idle unless noted.

div.div: Legend

g.text: Cell fill = severity: green ≈1 (immune) · orange ~2× · red ≥2.5× or tail blow-up · yellow = capacity/bound-dependent
‡ = measured below the 0.90 co-execution overlap gate -> a LOWER BOUND; sustained co-tenancy is at least this bad [B.8]
All numbers measured this campaign; Orin in parentheses where it differs from Thor.
Takeaway: the one-sided asymmetry — compute starves memory (4.19×), memory barely touches compute (1.12×) — means a tiny control net cannot safely share an unmanaged context [B.6].

Sources (from constants.json / notes, not retyped): [B.1] copy-engine/DRAM-direction Table B.1.1 (same-dir 1.58–1.69, opposed 1.03, memset 2.33->4.01) · [B.4] controller_contention_peak, lockout_onset_occupancy · [B.6] interference matrix S cells (IM|IC 4.19/2.66, IC||IC 1.97, L2-eviction bound 15.5) · [B.5] bandwidth cliff ~120/50 GB/s · [B.8] WBC p99 Table B.8.1 (1.70, 0.64, 5.9 ms = 141×), overlap gate.
